name: Mt. Gox
technique: Hot wallet drained over years; insolvency hidden
rootCause: Mt. Gox, then handling ~70% of BTC volume, lost ~850,000 BTC. The hot wallet private key (wallet.dat) was stolen around 2011 and funds were siphoned for years without the books being reconciled. "Transaction malleability" was blamed publicly but explained very little of the loss. Lesson: proof of reserves and reconciliation.

MtGox was hacked. Losses totalled 850,000 BTC, worth $470m at the time.

Mt. Gox, once the dominant Bitcoin exchange, was systematically looted between 2011 and its collapse in February 2014. Poor private key management, inadequate internal controls, and custodial weaknesses enabled attackers to steal approximately 850,000 BTC, worth about $470 million at the time. The loss went undetected for years due to reconciliation failures and ended with the exchange's insolvency, bankruptcy, and a drawn-out creditor recovery process. Long-term theft enabled by compromised private keys, weak custodial practices, and lack of reconciliation or internal security controls at Mt. Gox.
